what: Add a third challenge measure, gym visits (check-ins), next to workouts logged and kg lifted
why: A monthly challenge can only count workouts or kg logged in the MettleUp app, so members who never log workouts (most gym members) can never take part, while the gym already keeps every check-in
impact_why: Attendance is what keeps a member paying; a visits challenge reaches every member with a QR or desk check-in, not only app loggers
my_view: My view: build this first among challenge changes. Attendance challenges ("come 16 times this month") are the standard club challenge in Glofox and Mindbody (as known by Jun 2026, not re-checked live). Count only timed check-ins, the same rule the busy hours already use, so an imported paper register cannot win.

what: Let the owner tick 'Repeat every month' on a challenge, so the server sets up next month's copy by itself
why: Today a challenge must be typed again every month (start today or later, at most 60 days ahead, two may not overlap), so a busy owner forgets and the gym goes without one
impact_why: One setting replaces a monthly task the owner has to remember; a monthly challenge only works as a habit if it never skips a month
my_view: My view: do it, with the copy made on the 25th so the owner can still change or cancel it before it starts. Strava runs its challenges as a fixed monthly series for the same reason (as known by Jun 2026, not re-checked live).

what: Let a member tap 'I did it' on the gym's workout of the day, and show the trainer how many did it today (and, for a timed or for-reps workout, a small result board)
why: The workout of the day only goes out: the server hands it to members and keeps nothing back, so the trainer never learns whether anyone did it
impact_why: Gives trainers a reason to keep posting it and members a daily reason to come in
my_view: My view: start with the count only ("14 did today's workout"); add the result board later if trainers ask. Wodify built its whole product on the workout-of-the-day result board (as known by Jun 2026, not re-checked live).

what: Send a phone pop-up when the trainer sends a new diet plan or records new body measurements
why: Pop-ups go out for plan request answers, report requests and shop orders, but a diet plan or new measurements wait silently until the member happens to open the right page
impact_why: The trainer's work is only worth something to the member who sees it; this reuses the existing note sender
my_view: My view: do it. Two more triggers of the same kind as the three already there, one short line each, opening the Body or Diet page. Members with pop-ups off are not touched.

what: When the owner adds a special day to the gym hours (closed for Diwali, short hours), send members one automatic pop-up the evening before
why: Special days are saved with the hours but only show if the member opens Gym timings; today the owner must also send a separate 'gym closed' message, which from the 3rd message of the day gives no pop-up
impact_why: A member who travels to a closed gym is the most annoyed member of the month; a day the owner already typed does the telling
my_view: My view: do it, as a gym-hours note outside the 10-a-day message count, only for days set at least a day ahead. It also removes the need to send the closed-day message by hand.

what: Let a member write one short follow-up under the trainer's reply to 'Ask a trainer', and let the trainer answer it once more
why: A question gets exactly one reply and then closes; a member who did not understand must start a new question, which counts against 3 a day and loses the context
impact_why: Most form and diet questions need one clarifying turn; a short thread keeps it in one place for the trainer
my_view: My view: allow one follow-up and one more reply, no more, so it stays 'ask a trainer' and never becomes a chat the trainer must watch all day. Trainerize keeps two-way trainer messages as a core feature (as known by Jun 2026, not re-checked live).

what: Let the owner set pause rules once (for example up to 15 days, once per plan, asked 3 days ahead), and approve pause requests inside those rules without a desk tap
why: Every pause request waits for someone at the desk to approve it, even the plain ones the owner would always say yes to
impact_why: Removes a daily desk task and gives the member an answer at once
my_view: My view: wait. First count how many pause requests gyms really get; if it is a few a month, the desk tap is fine. If it is many, build it, keeping the desk's own freeze path as the only way a plan moves. Member self-serve freeze within club rules is common in Mindbody and Glofox (as known by Jun 2026, not re-checked live).

what: After HQ confirms a Pay MettleUp payment, give the owner a downloadable receipt (and a GST invoice once MettleUp is GST registered) on the same page
why: A confirmed payment only moves the plan date; the owner gets no paper to show their accountant, and a GST-registered gym cannot claim the tax back without an invoice
impact_why: Indian business owners expect an invoice for every software bill; without one some will not pay by bank transfer
my_view: My view: do the plain receipt now (gym name, plan, amount, reference, dates, from the payment ledger). The GST invoice needs MettleUp's own GST number first, which is his call, not a build step.

what: Send the member a pop-up when a friend they invited joins and the gym adds the free days ('A friend you invited joined. 7 free days added')
why: The member who shared the invite only learns about it if they open the Gym tab and read a number; the moment that rewards sharing passes unseen
impact_why: A visible reward is what makes a member share the link a second time
my_view: My view: do it, with no friend's name in the pop-up (the server's own privacy rule says the member learns a count, never who). Fire it when the desk accepts the free days, not when the enquiry arrives.
